name: Australia
genZNote: Australia is the only country that's also an entire continent — and it's home to more venomous snake species than anywhere else on Earth, plus a marsupial-dominated ecosystem that evolved in near-total isolation for tens of millions of years.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The world's smallest continent and sixth-largest country by area, surrounded by the Indian and Pacific Oceans.
Predominantly arid or semi-arid ('the Outback'), with the vast majority of its population concentrated in coastal cities, especially in the southeast.
Home to unique ecosystems including the Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system, and extensive desert interior.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: English is the de facto national language; Indigenous Australian (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander) cultures represent one of the world's oldest continuous living cultures, dating back over 60,000 years.
A highly multicultural society built substantially through post-WWII immigration from Europe, and more recently from Asia, including a significant and growing Indian diaspora.
Sport (cricket, Australian Rules football, rugby, swimming) holds a central place in national identity and culture.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; the British monarch is head of state (represented by a Governor-General), while an elected Prime Minister leads the government.
Composed of six states and several territories, each with significant self-governing powers under Australia's federal system.
Federated as a single nation in 1901, uniting previously separate British colonies into the Commonwealth of Australia.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A significant global contributor to medical research, including the development of the cervical cancer vaccine (Gardasil) and cochlear implant technology.
Home to world-class astronomical research facilities, benefiting from clear, dark southern-hemisphere skies.
Strong mining engineering and resource extraction technology, given its position as a major global exporter of minerals.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A member of the Quad (alongside India, the US, and Japan) and AUKUS (with the US and UK), reflecting its central role in Indo-Pacific security.
A member of the Commonwealth of Nations and a close security ally of the United States.
An active participant in Pacific regional diplomacy and a significant contributor to international development assistance in the Pacific Islands region.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Australia share a 'Comprehensive Strategic Partnership', with both countries members of the Quad grouping focused on a free and open Indo-Pacific.
Home to a large and rapidly growing Indian diaspora, and Australia is a top destination for Indian international students.
A landmark India-Australia trade agreement (ECTA, 2022) has significantly boosted bilateral trade, alongside strong critical minerals and defence cooperation.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A highly developed, resource-rich economy strong in mining exports (iron ore, coal, lithium, natural gas), agriculture, and education services.
One of the world's largest exporters of iron ore and coal, key inputs for global steel and energy production.
A major destination for international education, particularly for Indian and Chinese students, forming a significant services export sector.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the only country that is also an entire continent.
Unique wildlife including kangaroos, koalas, and the world's largest coral reef system (the Great Barrier Reef).
Being a member of the Quad alongside India, and a top destination for Indian students.
One of the world's oldest continuous Indigenous cultures.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Australian Dollar (AUD).
Resource-driven economy — a top global exporter of iron ore, coal, and natural gas, alongside strong agriculture and services sectors.
One of the world's largest gold producers and a major wool exporter.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to the Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Exceptional marsupial biodiversity found almost nowhere else, including kangaroos, koalas, and wombats.
Vast arid 'Outback' interior; faces significant bushfire risk and is a leader in bushfire-management research.
Extensive network of national parks and marine protected areas.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have the world's longest continuous living culture, dating back over 60,000 years.
British colonization began in 1788 with the First Fleet's arrival at Sydney Cove.
Six British colonies federated into the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 January 1901.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1901 Federation under the Australian Constitution created a federal parliamentary system.
A constitutional monarchy — the British monarch is head of state, represented locally by a Governor-General.
1967 referendum overwhelmingly approved counting Aboriginal Australians in the census and allowing federal laws for them.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Australian Space Agency established in 2018 to coordinate national space activities.
Hosts major radio astronomy infrastructure, including the Parkes Observatory and part of the Square Kilometre Array project.
Strong innovation in mining technology and renewable energy (notably rooftop solar adoption).

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Strong sporting culture across cricket, rugby, swimming, and Australian Rules Football.
The Sydney Opera House is a UNESCO World Heritage-listed architectural icon.
Hosted the 2000 Sydney Summer Olympics.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the UN, G20, APEC, and the Commonwealth of Nations.
Part of the Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) alongside India, the US, and Japan, and the AUKUS security partnership with the US and UK.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Australia is a federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy that is also the world's only country-continent, a Quad member and major trade/education partner for India.
keyFacts: Capital: Canberra (not Sydney). Currency: Australian Dollar.
Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; British monarch is head of state.
Federated in 1901, uniting separate British colonies.
Member of the Quad (with India, US, Japan) and AUKUS (with US, UK).
commonConfusion: Australia's capital is Canberra, not Sydney or Melbourne — Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise capital between the two larger rival cities.

highYieldFacts: Australia: federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; capital Canberra; federated in 1901.
Quad member with India, US, Japan; also part of AUKUS with US and UK.
India-Australia: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership; ECTA trade agreement (2022); top destination for Indian students.
commonTraps: Assuming Sydney is Australia's capital — it is Canberra.
Confusing Australia's Quad membership (with India, US, Japan) with its separate AUKUS pact (with US, UK only).
mustRemember: Australia: country-continent, federal constitutional monarchy, Quad/AUKUS member, ECTA trade partner and top study destination for India.
